children: The Treasury Department announced that it will purchase a maximum of $6 billion of longer-term bonds at its buyback operation on Thursday, adding key details to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's effort to hold down bond yields.

The Treasury Department had already announced last month that it would at least double buybacks of longer-term bonds, expanding a program that was originally intended to improve liquidity in older, less frequently traded securities. The first operation since last month's announcement-specifically focused on 10-year to 20-year Treasurys-will take place Thursday from 1:40 p.m. to 2 p.m. ET.
Recently, the Treasury Department has been buying a maximum of $2 billion of longer-term Treasurys per operation, so a maximum of $4 billion was the least that investors had expected.
This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).
